items.followUp: A block has a mass of 600 g and a volume of 150 cm³. Find its density in kg/m³.

rubric.why: The mass and volume are converted to SI units.
rubric.description: Convert the mass and volume to SI units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for converting to 0.8 kg and 2 × 10⁻⁴ m³ (or 0.0002 m³).

rubric.why: The density relation is used to obtain the correct SI answer.
rubric.description: Calculate the density and state its SI unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for using density = mass ÷ volume and obtaining 4000 kg/m³.

modelAnswer: Given: m = 800 g = 0.8 kg; V = 200 cm³ = 2 × 10⁻⁴ m³

items.followUp: Write Einstein’s mass-energy equation and state the value of the speed of light in vacuum.

rubric.why: This is the value of the speed of light in vacuum.

modelAnswer: Einstein’s mass-energy equation is E = mc².
The value of c, the speed of light in vacuum, is 3 × 10⁸ m/s.

items.followUp: Using a speed-time graph, derive the third equation of motion, v² = u² + 2as.

rubric.why: The gradient of the speed-time graph gives the acceleration and the first equation of motion.
rubric.description: Obtain the velocity relation from the graph’s gradient.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a = (v − u)/t and hence v = u + at.

rubric.why: Displacement is the area under the speed-time graph.
rubric.description: Express displacement as the area under the graph.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for s = ½(u + v)t, identifying it as the trapezium area.

rubric.why: This substitutes the graph-derived relation v = u + at into the displacement expression.
rubric.description: Substitute the velocity relation into the area expression.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for s = ½(u + u + at)t.

rubric.why: This is the second equation of motion obtained by simplifying the substitution.
rubric.description: State the proved second equation of motion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for s = ut + ½at².

modelAnswer: Draw a speed-time graph with time t on the horizontal axis and speed on the vertical axis; show a straight line from (0, u) to (t, v).
The gradient of the graph is a = (v − u)/t, so v = u + at.
The displacement s is the area under the graph: s = area of trapezium = ½(u + v)t.
Substitute v = u + at: s = ½(u + u + at)t.
